slides.title: A Registry, Precisely Defined
bullets: An organized system collecting uniform data for a defined population
Defined by a specific disease, condition, or exposure
Serves a predetermined scientific, clinical, or policy purpose
AHRQ's classic definition, and a richly underused MSL tool

slides.title: What Only a Registry Can Do
bullets: Maps natural history and phenotypic diversity of a disease
Especially vital in rare disease, where no single center sees enough
Sharpens case definitions, risk stratification, severity prediction
Shows real long-term impact of preventive and therapeutic strategies
Informs clinical guidelines and health policy decisions

slides.title: Pooling Data Across Borders
bullets: Often coordinated at European or international scale
Pools patients across countries to reach a usable sample size
Considered a key evidence-based-medicine instrument in rare disease

slides.title: Longitudinal by Design
bullets: Combines retrospective and prospective data collection
Exams, labs, treatments, outcomes, increasingly patient-reported outcomes
Captures quality-of-life measures alongside clinical data
Reveals natural history no cross-sectional design could show

slides.title: Where Registries Create Value
bullets: Prime source for identifying genuine, specific evidence gaps
A natural collaboration point with scientific societies and patient groups
Feed secondary analyses for publications, congresses, the Medical Plan

slides.title: Know Your Registries, Proactively
bullets: Know what registries exist in your own therapeutic area
Know who manages them and what variables they collect
Know how to access analyses or propose a collaboration
Treat this as an active competency, not a reactive one

takeaway.title: Registries capture natural history and pool rare-disease data at a scale no single study can, and MSLs should track them proactively
bullets: Their longitudinal design reveals what cross-sectional studies cannot
They are a direct route to evidence gaps and society collaborations
Knowing your area's registries is an active, ongoing competency
